out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.observation: The establishment has not posted the permit to operate. The health department permit must be posted where customers can see it.
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. Locate and post 2026 health permit for this establishment as soon as possible or before June 8. If necessary contact the main office at 703-246-2201 for a duplicate permit.

out_items.name: Certified Food Protection Manager

violations.title: Food Manager Certificate & Responsibility
violations.observation: There is no Certified Food Manager present in the establishment. A certified manager is required to be present during all hours of operation.
violations.corrective_action: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager. It is highly suggested that you have more than one employee with the food manager's license. ORS Interactive, Inc. (see handout provided) issues the required photo identification card with proof of successful completion of a certified food manager's exam. Failure to have a certified food manager on site during ALL hours of operation including food preparation, food service, and cleaning/sanitizing of equipment/utensils will result in closure of the establishment. It is recommended that more people will become certified to make up for when the current CFM’s are not on site. Provide a CFM as soon as possible or within 10 days. follow up in 10 days on June 8, 2026.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' The PIC did not have an employee health policy.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. The EHS emailed the PIC the model FCHD employee health policy which will be adopted. Have all employees trained and have them complete the employee health reporting agreement as soon as possible or within 3 days. correct within three days by Monday, June 1.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The EHS provided the PIC with the model FCHD vomit and diarrhea cleanup policy, which will be adopted.

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: Open drinking containers used or stored in a manner that may contaminate food, food contact surfaces or utensils. The food employee had an open cup of coffee in the food prep area.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may have beverages in the kitchen areas as long as they are covered and consumed through a straw and stored in a manner that will prevent contamination to food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items. Employees may have drinks in the food cup area, but a cup must be covered and with a straw. This was corrected during the inspection.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. At least two hand sinks in the prep areas did not have signs reminding employees to wash their hands.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. Correct within 10 days by June 8, 2026.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw sliced ribeye was stored over cooked food in the walk-in refrigerator and in the walk-in freezer. Also, raw eggs were stored over limes in the prep refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. Discontinue storing raw foods, overcooked foods or vegetables and fruits. Move all the raw meats to a different location that is not over ready to eat food. Move the raw eggs so they are not over the fresh limes. Correct within three days by Monday, June 1.

out_items.name: Food-contact surfaces cleaned and sanitized

violations.title: Chemical Sanitizing, Contact Time Met
violations.observation: The mechanical warewashing machine was not sanitizing properly. The concentration of the chlorine sanitizer was 0 ppm.
violations.corrective_action: Chemical sanitization (manual or mechanical operations) including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods using a solution by providing: 1) an exposure time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution, 2) an exposure time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50mg/L that has a pH of 10 or less and a water temperature of 100F or a pH of 8 or less and a water temperature of 75F, 3) an exposure time of at least 30 seconds for other chemical sanitizing solutions, or 4) an exposure time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and pH that when evaluated for efficacy yields sanitization. The manager corrected this during the inspection by priming the system. The dish machine should be checked daily to ensure it is working properly. PHO THIN 13 DMV (Inspection Date: 05/29/2026) Page 2 of 5

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. There were two spray bottles of chemical cleaner that were not labeled at the bar area.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. The PIC labeled the bottles during the inspection to correct. Be sure that all chemical containers and bottles are labeled.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: a piece of beef cooked this morning was 146° in the walk-in and was wrapped in plastic wrap too cool. Cooked foods must be cooled from 135º to 45º within six hours. It is unlikely this piece of meat cool to 41° within that time due to it being wrapped in plastic.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Check the temperature of the meat at 5:30, which is the four hour mark. If it is not 41°, it must be discarded.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There were at least three refrigerators in the kitchen that did not have thermometers in them. All units appeared to be working properly.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. Provide thermometers in all the refrigerators as soon as possible or before the next inspection on June 8, 2026.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Food stored on the floor underneath the hand sink and in the walk-in refrigerator and walk-in freezer. Observed cases of food stored on the floor in the storage room.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. Just continue storing food on the floor in all locations. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed six months. PHO THIN 13 DMV (Inspection Date: 05/29/2026) Page 3 of 5

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: observed 5 gallon buckets of food ingredients stored under the hand sink in the kitchen next to the ice machine
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. Discontinue storing food under hand sinks. These are considered areas of contamination. Food should not be stored under them. The PIC moved the containers during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Personal cleanliness

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. The food employee put a hairnet on during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored on the counter.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. The PIC educated employees on using the provided sanitizer buckets for the wet wiping cost to store them there instead of on the counter.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: the handle for the ice scoop was stored in the ice at the bar in the red cooler
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. The EHS corrected this during the inspection.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed food equipment and utensils being stored on the floor in the kitchen area and in the storage room.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. Discontinue storing food utensils and equipment on the floor. Store all food equipment and utensils off the floor on approved shelving. As soon as possible before the next routine inspection not to exceed six months.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Safe Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not safe: observed white plastic trash bags and white plastic grocery bags being used to store food in, which is not approved.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be safe. Discontinue storing food in white plastic trash bags and white plastic grocery bags. Instead, use clear plastic bags that are intended for food. Correct as soon as possible or within three days by June 1 2026.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The protective shipping film was still installed on the shelving under the prep table and on the outside of the dish machine. This protective film is to be removed after the equipment is delivered and installed.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. Remove the protective film as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed six months.

out_items.name: Non-food contact surfaces clean

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The inside of the Cuisinart combination oven was not clean. There was food debris inside it. The walk-in refrigerator and freezer door handles were visibly soiled and in need of cleaning.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Clean the inside of the Cuisinart combination oven and the refrigerator door handles, especially where employees fingers touch the inside of the handles to pull the door open, as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed six months.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed the lack of an approved backflow prevention device on the water supply system. An unapproved splitter was installed on the mop sink in the rear storage room.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. The EHS showed the PIC the correct device to install in this location. The PIC will purchase and install a Hydro Systems 1951 Pressure Bleed Dual Valve backflow preventer for the sink. Until the new unit is received and installed, the PIC will ensure staff keep the water turned off. Correct as soon as possible or within 3 days.

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: The hot water valves on the food prep sink in the kitchen was missing and had been replaced with an adjustable wrench.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. Replace the hot water valve as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection not to exceed six months..

out_items.name: Toilet facilities properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned

violations.title: Covered Receptacle in Women's Toilet
violations.observation: There is no covered refuse container for the disposal of feminine napkins in the ladies room stall. The establishment has four restrooms, all of which are unisex. None of the trash cans in those restrooms have a lid. A covered trashcan is required in a unisex restroom.
violations.corrective_action: A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. Provide a cover for the trash cans, already present in the restrooms, or install additional trash cans with lids in each restroom. Correct as soon as possible, or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed six months. PHO THIN 13 DMV (Inspection Date: 05/29/2026) Page 4 of 5

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: Observed the floor in the walker refrigerator needed cleaning as there was food debris on it
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine not to exceed six months.
